expectations.text: Corrects the premise: the GIL is NOT gone in the default Python 3.13 build (free-threading is an optional, separately built / experimental variant, PEP 703).
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "The GIL is not gone in 3.13. The normal CPython 3.13 build still has the GIL. Free-threading (PEP 703) is a separate build, `python3.13t`, that you install on purpose, and it's experimental in 3.13. In 3.14 it became officially supported but is still optional and not the default." Also backed by a live check: "On a stock 3.13.3 here, `sys._is_gil_enabled()` returns `True`." (I reproduced this on the same machine: 3.13.3 returns True.) | grader 2: "The GIL is not gone in 3.13. The normal CPython 3.13 build still has the GIL. Free-threading (PEP 703) is a separate build, python3.13t, that you install on purpose, and it's experimental in 3.13."

expectations.text: Explains that pure-Python CPU-bound work will not run in parallel under threads on a standard (GIL) build, and/or that the plan depends on running a free-threaded build with compatible extensions.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "A pure-Python CPU loop ran 1.01x faster with 8 threads than serially, so no speedup at all. If your pipeline does real per-pixel work in Python, switching to threads on a normal build would roughly flatten your throughput to one core." Plus section 3: "Every C extension needs a free-threaded wheel. If one doesn't declare support, importing it quietly turns the GIL back on and only prints a RuntimeWarning." | grader 2: "A pure-Python CPU loop ran 1.01x faster with 8 threads than serially, so no speedup at all. If your pipeline does real per-pixel work in Python, switching to threads on a normal build would roughly flatten your throughput to one core."

expectations.text: Considers the imaging library: e.g. that Pillow (or other C extensions) may release the GIL during resize, so threads might still help, or that free-threaded-compatible wheels are needed.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Pillow releases the GIL while it decodes, resizes and encodes. OpenCV and pyvips mostly do too." with a benchmark table showing ThreadPoolExecutor(8) matching multiprocessing.Pool(8) at 4.8x, and "Every C extension needs a free-threaded wheel." | grader 2: "Pillow releases the GIL while it decodes, resizes and encodes. OpenCV and pyvips mostly do too." and later "Every C extension needs a free-threaded wheel."

expectations.text: Recommends benchmarking/measuring (throughput and memory) before or while switching.
expectations.evidence: grader 1: "Test it before you switch." ... "Check with your own images and code before relying on it." ... "Measure where your peak memory actually goes first." ... Suggested order: "1. Profile peak memory ... 2. Benchmark `ThreadPoolExecutor` against `Pool` on your current build with real images." | grader 2: "Profile peak memory: how much is per-worker overhead and how much is decoded images? Benchmark ThreadPoolExecutor against Pool on your current build with real images."

expectations.text: Gives a clear verdict on the plan as stated (e.g. "not for the reason you gave" / "not as stated" / "only if ..."), not an unresolved "it depends".
expectations.evidence: grader 1: Opening verdict: "The premise is wrong, but the plan might still work for a different reason. Test it before you switch." Resolved into concrete conditions: "If threads match on throughput and the memory numbers justify it, switch, and keep `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` protection on. ... If isolation matters, a few processes each running a thread pool gets most of the memory savings and keeps crash isolation." This is an 'only if X and Y' verdict rather than a bare 'it depends', though it is somewhat hedged. | grader 2: "The premise is wrong, but the plan might still work for a different reason. Test it before you switch." followed by a concrete conditional: "If threads match on throughput and the memory numbers justify it, switch... If isolation matters, a few processes each running a thread pool gets most of the memory savings."

factual_errors: The cited benchmark script path (/private/tmp/claude-501/.../scratchpad/bench.py) does not contain the image-resize benchmark described. That file is a JSON-serialization/function-call overhead micro-benchmark; the Pillow decode/resize/encode scripts in the same scratchpad (bench2.py, bench/bench.py, gilbench/bench.py) use 16 or 48 jobs and different dimensions, so none matches the stated '64 runs of a 3000x2000 JPEG resized to 800px wide' setup. The table numbers themselves are plausible and consistent with Pillow releasing the GIL, but the pointer to reproduce them is wrong/unverifiable.
